title: UniCoS: A Unified Neural and Accelerator Co-Search Framework for CNNs and ViTs
problem: Current algorithm-hardware co-search methods suffer from lengthy training times and inadequate exploration of hardware design spaces, resulting in suboptimal joint architecture-accelerator solutions.
motivation: Co-optimization of neural networks and hardware accelerators is critical for achieving energy-efficient AI, but existing methods waste time on full retraining and miss promising hardware configurations.
method: UniCoS uses a training-free accuracy proxy—a method that predicts how well a network will perform in seconds without actually training it—to quickly evaluate candidate CNN and ViT architectures. It combines this with a clustering-based algorithm that explores heterogeneous hardware dataflows (different patterns for how computations can be organized in accelerators). Together, these enable rapid joint searching: finding the best combination of network architecture and accelerator design at the same time.
key_novelty: A training-free accuracy proxy that predicts network performance in seconds (without full training) combined with clustering-based exploration of hardware dataflows enables rapid co-search of both CNN and ViT architectures with their accelerators.
contributions: Training-free proxy achieving accuracy evaluation in seconds versus hours of full training
Clustering-based algorithm for exploring heterogeneous dataflow designs
Unified framework supporting both CNNs and Vision Transformers achieving 3.54x EDP improvement with 1.76% higher accuracy on ImageNet in 3 hours
limitations: Specific baseline names and detailed hardware design space scope not provided.
primary_theme: Training-free neural and accelerator co-search for CNNs and ViTs
